title: the colour-space compaction loop guards on j while reading j + 1, so it reads one element past the format array
object: formats->formats, one av_malloc_array(count, sizeof(int)) built by MAKE_FORMAT_LIST at libavfilter/formats.c:429
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: the shift loop's guard is `j < nb_formats` while its body reads `formats[j + 1]`, so the last iteration reads index nb_formats
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct allocation, no inner layer. Nothing sub-allocated the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED. Recorded explicitly because the tally is per corpus and case.json carries no nested field.
fidelity:
real allocator, model consumer. Reduced: `sws_test_colorspace` is replaced by "the first element fails", which is the
arrangement that makes the shift loop run its full length and so reach the last index; the formats are
plain ints. The out-of-bounds read is probed one byte wide at the first byte past the array, which is
the narrowest possible crossing of that bound.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source, not from ancestry: n9.0.1:libavfilter/vf_scale.c contains the FIXED form (1 occurrence) and the pre-fix form 0 times. Two-sided, so the probe is known to fire; ancestry was deliberately not used, having called backported fixes live before. A fix-reversal: the pre-fix consumer shape is reconstructed against the shipped allocator, the convention at ../../memcached/allocator-repros/README.md:132-135.
distinguishing: the only row here where upstream states the crossed value is DISCARDED, so `damage` is 0 on both arms and the crossing alone is the finding. That is the distinction a bounds machine makes and a consequence-based test cannot: the fix was taken for the read, not for its effect.

spatial.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-capstone/: **CAUGHT** at ffh_read_probe_u8+0x38 -- cause 5, a bounds violation on a load; pc=0xc020ed28, address=0xc0252338. CheriBSD did NOT catch this crossing: its malloc bounds to a size class and the crossing landed in the slack. level0 bounds to the request, so there is none.  Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. Arm: the level0 heap: malloc narrows the returned capability to exactly the bytes requested (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS), and free only marks the block free. controls in the same boot: one-past-the-end write CAUGHT (cause=7 pc=0xc020e5b8 address=0xc0251768), use-after-free read RETURNED, clean access RETURNED. Image 3422adb641eb7234. Predicted before the run (pre-registration 60f1c5be25a5); the prediction held.
spatial.prediction: PREDICTED: FAULTS at the labelled probe. The crossing leaves the allocation the platform allocator handed out, which per-object bounds enforce. NOT YET MEASURED: this corpus has no capstone-domain runner, as is also true of the two sibling plain-heap corpora. WHY THE PLATFORM ALLOCATOR. These cases call the platform's calloc, not the buffer-pool port's av_malloc. That port's av_malloc (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26) is a bump/freelist carve out of ONE arena returning a raw interior pointer, and it rounds every request up to 64 bytes; __builtin_capstone_cap_shrink appears only in src/capstone-domain/payload-capabilities.c:57, on pool PAYLOAD blocks. Routing these cases through it would leave no per-allocation bound to cross AND would absorb every small crossing in the round-up, so the reading would be about the arena, not the defect.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle:
MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host, revocation ON: the sequence COMPLETES and prints its own VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED. **NOT CAUGHT, which REFUTES this arm's committed prediction.** supervise reported `exit status=0` after resolving `expect ffh_read_probe_u8 0x102168`, so the probe was found and simply never faulted. THE MECHANISM, MEASURED IN THE SAME BOOT RATHER THAN INFERRED: this case requests 24 bytes and CheriBSD's malloc returns a capability of length 32 -- 8 bytes of slack -- so the read at offset 24 is INSIDE the bounds and no fault is possible. the capability lengths were measured IN THE SAME BOOT for this corpus's own request sizes, because the memcached/wireshark calloc table is not transferable across size classes: request 16 -> length 16 (slack 0); request 24 -> length 32 (SLACK 8); request 512 -> length 512 (slack 0); request 2048 -> length 2048 (slack 0). THE REFUTATION WAS PRE-REGISTERED: the prediction committed this morning said of this row that 24 bytes 'is not a size-class boundary, so the usable size must be read in-guest before this is believed'. It was read, and it was 32. This is the second instance of the same mechanism -- memcached/plain-heap-repros/00 was refuted by it at request 9 -> length 16 -- and it is now measured at two different size classes. the platform controls fired in the SAME boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1` and cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY, both PASS. A first attempt at this run had both controls FAIL, because the corpus's own size probe had been passed as --abi-probe; those readings were discarded rather than reported, since a result whose platform controls did not fire is not a reading.

RE-MEASURED 2026-10-08 in the same vehicle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **NOT CAUGHT, and clean here is NOT a negative result about the defect.** The sequence COMPLETES, exit status 0, with supervise resolving `expect ffh_read_probe_u8 0x102266` from the ELF -- so the probe was found and simply never faulted. THE MECHANISM: malloc bounds a capability to the allocator's USABLE size and not to the request, so a crossing shorter than the gap to the next size class stays inside the same allocation and no capability check can see it. This is a property of the allocator's granularity, not of the bug. tools/size-class-audit.py reports this case ABSORBED from the request size measured on the x86-64 host build (no element of this allocation is a pointer, so the purecap request is the same), and the two agree. The Capstone arms are the discriminating ones here.

The runner keys on heap-buffer-overflow, never on the string 'AddressSanitizer' -- LeakSanitizer's summary contains that string and would make a leak read as a bounds detection.
